original_abstract.text: Embedding models compress variable-length text into fixed-size vector representations, but this compression can entangle semantic content with residual token-level information, such as artifacts arising from attention sink behavior. We propose a simple method that prepends trainable [DUMP] tokens to the input during embedding model training. The method keeps the model architecture, pooling strategy, and training loss unchanged, while optimizing the added tokens through the standard contrastive retrieval objective. By introducing trainable prefix positions that interact with regular tokens during encoding, [DUMP] tokens help reduce the influence of residual or uninformative token-level signals on the final retrieval representation. Experiments on standard retrieval and long-context benchmarks show that our method consistently improves over finetuned baselines across encoder and decoder embedding models. Further analysis shows that [DUMP] tokens alter token-level activation and attention patterns associated with low-information tokens. These results suggest that trainable prefix tokens provide a lightweight way to improve retrieval representations.
original_abstract.source_title: Reducing Representational Interference in Retrieval Embeddings with Trainable Prefix Tokens

en.text: The method prepends trainable [DUMP] tokens during embedding-model training to reduce residual, low-information token signals in the final retrieval representation. The backbone, pooling and loss remain unchanged; the added prefixes learn through the standard contrastive retrieval objective. Tests on standard and long-context retrieval benchmarks improve over fine-tuned baselines for both encoder and decoder embedding models. The approach provides a lightweight retrieval-representation intervention, rather than a scaling law or a demonstrated recommendation-system gain.

zh.text: 该方法在嵌入模型训练时加入可训练的 [DUMP] 前缀 token，减弱低信息量 token 的残余信号对最终检索向量的干扰。骨干结构、池化方式和损失保持不变，前缀通过原有对比检索目标学习。标准检索和长上下文检索实验中，encoder 与 decoder 嵌入模型均优于对应微调基线。它提供了轻量的检索表征修正方法，尚未建立扩展规律或验证推荐系统收益。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation retrieves items by autoregressively generating Semantic IDs(SIDs), where an RQ-VAE quantizes each item into a hierarchical SID sequence that the decoder generates level by level. We identify an overlooked bottleneck in this paradigm: the Semantic Quantization Gap(SQG). Quantization derives SIDs from rich continuous signals, including codebook centroids, local neighborhood geometry, and level-wise entropy. However, the decoder receives only discrete identifiers and loses the semantic structure that shaped them. This mismatch manifests in three ways: a grounding gap, where the decoder lacks semantic anchors when target-side information is limited; a neighborhood gap, where token-level supervision discards inter-item similarity and exacerbates exposure bias; and a difficulty gap, where computation is allocated uniformly despite generation difficulty diminishing with depth. To bridge the SQG, we propose BRIDGE. Codebook-grounded latent reasoning injects frozen quantizer centroids as semantic anchors before SID generation. Privileged EMA self-distillation transfers neighborhood-aware knowledge from a teacher to an on-policy student, preserving inter-item geometry while mitigating exposure bias. Effort-aware recurrence allocates more computation to the challenging early levels and progressively reduces it with depth. Across three Amazon benchmarks, BRIDGE improves Recall@10 and NDCG@10 by 10.9% and 9.7% on average over the strongest baseline (up to 12.6% and 10.7%). In a one-week online A/B experiment on a large-scale e-commerce advertising platform with 5% traffic, BRIDGE improves eCPM by 0.65%.
original_abstract.source_title: BRIDGE: Bridging the Semantic Quantization Gap for Generative Recommendation

en.text: BRIDGE addresses the semantic information lost when a generative recommender sees only discrete semantic IDs. It supplies frozen codebook centroids as reasoning anchors, distills neighborhood structure through a privileged EMA teacher and allocates more recurrent computation to difficult early ID levels. Across three Amazon benchmarks, average Recall@10 and NDCG@10 improve by 10.9% and 9.7% over the strongest baseline. A one-week, 5%-traffic e-commerce advertising A/B test reports a 0.65% eCPM gain. The method suggests preserving quantizer geometry and varying compute by ID depth; the abstract gives no matched-budget efficiency result.

zh.text: BRIDGE处理生成推荐只接收离散语义ID、丢失量化阶段连续语义信息的问题。它把冻结的码本质心作为推理锚点，用带额外信息的EMA教师蒸馏邻域结构，并给较难的ID前几层分配更多循环计算。在三个Amazon数据集上，相对最强基线，Recall@10和NDCG@10平均提高10.9%和9.7%；电商广告平台一周、5%流量的A/B测试报告eCPM提高0.65%。可借鉴的是保留量化几何信息并按ID深度分配计算，摘要未给出等预算效率结论。

original_abstract.text: Attention is a core building block of frontier models and often dominates compute-bound prefill at long context. FP8 matrix instructions offer twice the peak throughput of BF16, but they accelerate only matrix multiplication, and the softmax between the two matrix multiplications of attention runs on vector units that FP8 does not accelerate. On the AMD Instinct MI355X, the vendor's AITER kernels reach 39% of peak FP8 matrix throughput at 32K tokens, compared with 49% in BF16. Attention is also more numerically sensitive to quantization than feed-forward layers, and unlike NVIDIA's Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, the MI355X does not track the completion of matrix instructions in hardware, so overlapping the softmax with the matrix multiplications depends on instruction order. We present ZYFA, prefill kernels for the MI355X built on three techniques: (1) computing each FP8 probability directly from its score with a multiply-add and an integer conversion instead of an exponential; (2) a ping-pong schedule in which one group of threads computes its softmax while another executes its matrix multiplications; and (3) scaling each block of probabilities up by a power of two before rounding, and normalizing by the sum of the rounded probabilities. On attention inputs captured from three models and timed at sustained clock speeds, ZYFA achieves 1.16-1.76x the throughput of AITER. On the Gaussian inputs of kernel benchmarks at 32K tokens, it achieves 1.26-1.37x at head dimension 128 and 1.99x for DeepSeek-style multi-head latent attention. The sustained clock of the MI355X depends on operand values, so throughput on random inputs does not reliably predict throughput on real model activations. At head dimension 128, ZYFA's numerical error is within a few percent of that of Composable Kernel and Triton and 62-78% lower than that of AITER's. The source code is available at https://github.com/Zyphra/zyfa.
original_abstract.source_title: ZYFA: Speed and Accuracy of FP8 FlashAttention on AMD CDNA4

en.text: ZYFA targets the softmax and scheduling bottlenecks that limit FP8 attention on AMD MI355X. It combines direct score-to-FP8 probability conversion, overlapping matrix multiplication with softmax, and blockwise probability scaling before rounding. On activations captured from three models at sustained clock speeds, its prefill kernels deliver 1.16–1.76x AITER throughput. At head dimension 128, numerical error is close to Composable Kernel and Triton and lower than AITER. The paper also shows why random-input benchmarks can mispredict real-activation throughput on this hardware. This is a hardware-specific attention-kernel result, not an end-to-end recommendation speedup.

zh.text: ZYFA针对AMD MI355X上FP8注意力的softmax与调度瓶颈，直接把分数转换为FP8概率，让矩阵乘法与softmax交叠执行，并在舍入前按块缩放概率。在三个模型的真实激活、持续运行频率下，预填充核吞吐为AITER的1.16–1.76倍；head dimension为128时，数值误差接近Composable Kernel和Triton，低于AITER。论文还指出该硬件的频率受操作数影响，随机输入跑分不能可靠预测真实吞吐。可借鉴的是硬件协同设计与评测方法，并非已经验证的推荐端到端加速。

original_abstract.text: Semantic information can enrich the identifiers and structured fields used by recommender systems. Semantic tokenization provides a structured representation of this information by converting LLM-derived user profiles into discrete tokens. In the common two-stage pipeline, the tokenizer is trained before the recommender. Its token assignments are then treated as fixed input features during recommendation training. As a result, the downstream recommender can learn how to use the assigned indices, but it cannot revise the semantic partition that produced them. Making this partition task-aware is difficult because nearest-code assignment is discrete, and unconstrained adaptation may also distort the geometry learned during pretraining. Moreover, a fixed token depth exposes the same semantic resolution to every interaction. We thus propose OptST (Optimizing Semantic Tokenization), which makes a pretrained tokenizer responsive to downstream recommendation. To revise token assignments without directly updating the pretrained encoder or base codebooks, OptST learns a low-rank deformation whose drift is limited by an anchor regularizer. Recommendation supervision reaches this transformation through a straight-through estimator, while prediction retains hard nearest-code assignments. Beyond adapting the assignments themselves, OptST selects an interaction-conditioned prefix to control how much residual detail is exposed to the recommender. Experiments on four public datasets show that OptST achieves the highest AUC among conventional and LLM-enhanced baselines. Its improvements also persist across different recommendation backbones. These results establish task-aware semantic tokenization as an effective interface between LLM-derived profiles and downstream recommendation models.
original_abstract.source_title: OptST: Optimizing Semantic Tokenization for LLM-Enhanced Recommendation

en.text: OptST adapts semantic tokenization of LLM-derived user profiles to downstream recommendation. A regularized low-rank transformation changes token assignments while keeping the pretrained encoder and base codebooks fixed; a straight-through estimator supplies training gradients, and an interaction-conditioned prefix selects semantic detail. It reports the highest AUC among evaluated conventional and LLM-enhanced baselines on four public datasets, with gains across backbones. The transferable idea is a task-aware interface between profile semantics and recommendation features.

zh.text: OptST 让大模型用户画像的语义分词随推荐任务调整。它固定预训练编码器和基础码本，用受约束的低秩变换调整 token 分配；训练时通过直通估计器传递梯度，再按当前交互选择保留多少层语义细节。在四个公开数据集和多种推荐骨干上，方法取得优于所比较基线的 AUC。它为语义画像与推荐特征之间的任务适配提供了具体接口。

original_abstract.text: In large language model (LLM) serving systems, the key-value (KV) cache grows linearly with sequence length and concurrency, so long-context inference easily hits the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) capacity wall and results in low concurrency. Offloading the KV cache to host dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) frees HBM space and raises concurrency, but the additional cache management and host-to-device (H2D) load overhead inflates inference latency, higher concurrency fails to translate into effective throughput. We present FlashOffloading, a host-DRAM-centric inference architecture that fully offloads the KV cache in both the prefill and decode phases. FlashOffloading builds rolling HBM cache for prefill, a hot cache for decode, a reverse sparse index with zero extra miss-lookup overhead, and a compute--load overlapped kernel, optimizing KV offloading latency across the entire pipeline and delivering throughput gains under a time-per-output-token (TPOT) service-level objective (SLO). In experiments deploying GLM-5.2 with multi-token prediction (MTP3) speculative decoding on an Ascend910C prefill--decode (PD)-disaggregated platform, FlashOffloading improves prefill throughput by up to 1.38\(\times\) and decode throughput by up to 1.91\(\times\) under a 30 ms TPOT constraint. FlashOffloading is integrated into an open-source serving framework: this https URL.
original_abstract.source_title: FlashOffloading: Low-Latency KV Cache Offloading for Long-Context LLM Serving

en.text: FlashOffloading stores the complete key-value cache in host DRAM while using GPU or accelerator memory for a rolling working set. It overlaps bulk transfers during prefill and fetches sparse-index-selected entries during decode, reducing lookup and transfer overhead. GLM-5.2 experiments on Ascend 910C examine both phases under a latency target. The design may support longer recommendation histories under limited device memory, but the reported speedups are specific to the evaluated language-model system.

zh.text: FlashOffloading 将完整键值缓存放在主机 DRAM，设备显存只保留滚动工作集：预填充时重叠批量传输与计算，解码时只读取稀疏索引选中的位置，减少查找和搬运开销。论文在昇腾 910C 上用 GLM-5.2 评估延迟目标下的两阶段性能。该设计可启发有限显存下的长历史服务，现有加速结果属于所测语言模型系统。

original_abstract.text: Linear attention reduces the quadratic sequence-length complexity of softmax attention by maintaining fixed-size recurrent states. However, these states scale quadratically with the representation dimension and require repeated data transfers during decoding, creating a substantial GPU memory bottleneck. Recent studies have revealed significant low-rank redundancy in recurrent states, suggesting opportunities for more efficient representations. We introduce SPARE (State Projection for Accelerated Recurrent Execution), a training-free method that exploits this redundancy through fixed low-dimensional subspaces, heterogeneous rank allocation, and lightweight write compensation. By performing recurrent reads and updates directly on compact states, SPARE reduces memory traffic without online decomposition or dense-state reconstruction. SPARE achieves 2.55x full-model decoding speedup, 7.49x lower recurrent-kernel DRAM traffic, and 3.31x lower peak GPU memory, while preserving better associative-retrieval accuracy than structured pruning at matched memory budgets.
original_abstract.source_title: SPARE: Fast Linear Attention Decoding with Compact Recurrent States

en.text: SPARE targets the memory traffic of linear attention's recurrent states, whose size grows quadratically with representation width. Without retraining, it uses fixed low-dimensional subspaces, heterogeneous ranks and write compensation to read and update compressed states directly, avoiding online decomposition and dense reconstruction. The abstract reports 2.55x full-model decode speedup, 7.49x lower recurrent-kernel DRAM traffic and 3.31x lower peak GPU memory, but does not identify the speed baseline or hardware. Associative retrieval is better than structured pruning at matched memory budgets. The mechanism offers a candidate approach for compact long-history states.

zh.text: SPARE处理线性注意力递归状态随表示宽度平方增长、解码反复搬运状态的问题。它无需重新训练，用固定低维子空间、差异化秩分配和写入补偿直接读写压缩状态，省去在线分解与稠密状态重建。摘要报告整模型解码提速2.55倍、递归核DRAM流量降至约1/7.49、GPU峰值内存降至约1/3.31，但未说明速度基线和硬件。在相同内存预算下，其关联检索精度优于结构化剪枝；这一机制可作为长行为历史状态压缩的候选方案。

original_abstract.text: Collaborative-filtering (CF) scores provide graded, personalized rewards for training large language model (LLM) recommenders through reinforcement learning. However, these rewards can cause exposure collapse: even though the CF model itself produces diverse top recommendations across users, an LLM optimized with its rewards concentrates on fewer items. We decompose each score into an item-mean component, the item's average CF score across user histories, and a residual component, the current user's score deviation from the average. Through controlled interventions, we identify the item-mean component as a contributor to exposure collapse. Accordingly, we propose two reward corrections: per-item centering removes each item's estimated mean score, while per-item standardization further rescales the residual using its estimated standard deviation. Experiments on two datasets with two identifier schemes show that both corrections substantially improve catalog coverage and exposure evenness. Compared with training on the uncorrected CF reward, our corrections increase the number of distinct items ranked first across users by up to $9.8\times$, while maintaining comparable ranking accuracy. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/LLM4Rec-CF-Bias-27EF/.
original_abstract.source_title: What Gets Hacked in a Collaborative Reward for LLM Recommenders: The Part That Does Not Depend on the User

en.text: The study diagnoses exposure collapse when collaborative-filtering scores reward an LLM recommender during reinforcement learning. It separates an item’s average score across users from its user-specific residual, then centers or standardizes the reward per item. Controlled experiments on two datasets with two identifier schemes yield up to 9.8 times as many distinct top-ranked items as the uncorrected reward while retaining comparable ranking accuracy. The result offers a concrete reward-design check for generative recommendation, rather than a model-scaling law or an industrial deployment result.

zh.text: 这项研究分析了用协同过滤分数奖励大模型推荐器时的曝光集中现象。它把物品跨用户的平均分与当前用户的个性化残差分开，再按物品对奖励做中心化或标准化。在两个数据集、两种物品标识方案的受控实验中，排名首位的不同物品数最高达到未修正奖励时的 9.8 倍，同时保持相近的排序准确性。其借鉴点是检查生成式推荐奖励中与用户无关的分量，论文没有建立模型扩展定律或报告工业部署。

original_abstract.text: Re-ranking aims to present users with an ordered list that maximizes sequence-level utility. Industrial deployments widely adopt the Generator--Evaluator framework, where the generator proposes candidate sequences, and the evaluator scores them to select the best one for display. The fidelity of the evaluator's utility estimates thus directly governs recommendation quality. However, existing evaluators predominantly follow the \textbf{Independent Behavior Modeling (IBM)} paradigm, which simplifies the continuous user \emph{browsing journey} into independent per-item predictions (e.g., CTR). This oversimplification ignores two physical realities: (i) a click can occur only after the item has been reached and impressed, and (ii) items compete for finite user attention. As a result, IBM produces systematically biased evaluations and suboptimal sequence selection. To address this, we propose a \textbf{Joint Behavior Modeling (JBM)} perspective that explicitly models the \emph{display} $\rightarrow$ \emph{impression} $\rightarrow$ \emph{click} process to capture causal and competitive dependencies within a sequence. Building on JBM, we develop the \textbf{Impression-Click Evaluator (ICE)}, a plug-and-play framework that (i) predicts a browsing-depth distribution to estimate per-position impression probabilities, (ii) leverages predicted impressions to suppress spurious context from unexposed items during click modeling, and (iii) introduces a click distribution matching objective to capture intra-sequence dependencies. Extensive offline experiments across diverse backbones, together with a 14-day online A/B test in the Taobao App (+0.70\% clicks, +3.67\% revenue) and full-traffic deployment, validate the effectiveness and robustness of our approach.
original_abstract.source_title: Beyond Independent Predictions: Learning the Browsing Journey for Sequence-Level Re-ranking

en.text: ICE evaluates candidate recommendation lists by modeling display, impression and click jointly. It predicts browsing depth, uses impression probabilities to reduce context from unseen items, and matches the click distribution across the list. A 14-day Taobao A/B test reports 0.70% more clicks and 3.67% more revenue. This improves the evaluator in a generator–evaluator reranking pipeline; it addresses sequence utility rather than establishing a model-size scaling law.

zh.text: ICE 用“展示列表→用户实际看到→点击”的过程评估候选列表。它先预测浏览深度，再用曝光概率减弱未看到物品的干扰，并学习列表内的点击分布。淘宝 14 天线上实验报告点击量提升 0.70%、收入提升 3.67%。可借鉴点是改进生成器—评估器重排中的序列价值估计；论文没有建立模型规模的扩展规律。

original_abstract.text: ConvPE (Convolutional Position Embedding) improves both the performance and efficiency of Transformer models in language modeling, long-context extension, and vision. It injects a windowed, content-dependent bias into attention scores through a lightweight causal convolution over a low-dimensional projection of the hidden states. As a lightweight plug-in, ConvPE is compatible with RoPE, attention masks, and KV concatenation. It also supports high-dimensional position embeddings via high-dimensional convolutions. In a reproduction, ConvPE outperforms five 1D baselines and eight 2D baselines. The code is publicly available at this https URL.
original_abstract.source_title: ConvPE: Convolutional Position Embedding Improves Transformers

en.text: ConvPE adds a local, content-dependent bias to attention scores using a lightweight causal convolution over projected hidden states. It remains compatible with rotary position embeddings, attention masks and cache concatenation, and also supports higher-dimensional positional structure. Reported experiments cover language modeling, context extension and vision, with comparisons against one- and two-dimensional baselines. The plug-in offers a concrete way to combine local structure with attention for sequence models; recommendation gains have not been established.

zh.text: ConvPE 对投影后的隐藏状态做轻量因果卷积，向注意力分数加入依赖内容的局部偏置，同时兼容旋转位置编码、注意力掩码和缓存拼接，也支持更高维的位置结构。论文在语言建模、上下文扩展和视觉任务中与一维、二维基线比较。这种插件为序列模型结合局部结构与注意力提供了具体方法，尚无推荐收益验证。

original_abstract.text: LLM-based recommender systems increasingly generate chain-of-thought (CoT) text before each item prediction to activate the LLM's reasoning capacity, costing tens to hundreds of extra tokens per recommendation at inference. We ask whether inference-time reasoning artifacts (textual or latent) can be replaced by training-time supervision alone, without loss of accuracy. We propose LatentRec, a framework for LLM-based generative recommendation that replaces inference-time reasoning artifacts with training-time per-step head supervision. LatentRec has three components. A 2.5M-parameter Continuous Thought Module iterates K latent reasoning steps over the LLM's hidden state during training. Soft Token Selection bridges the ~14x norm gap between hidden states and input embeddings. A Per-step Reasoning Loss (PRL) supervises every intermediate state through the LLM's prediction head against the first token of the target Semantic ID. The trained LLM retains this accuracy without the module at inference, so the module can be discarded at deployment. On three Amazon benchmarks, LatentRec improves HR@10 by 4.0-5.0% (relative) over a CoT-distilled baseline at 18.3x lower latency (batch=1). Per-step training supervision consistently improves accuracy across three datasets, paid once at training rather than at every recommendation.
original_abstract.source_title: Do Recommenders Need to Think in Words? Latent Reasoning for Efficient LLM-Based Recommendation

en.text: LatentRec moves recommendation reasoning supervision into training to avoid generating extra reasoning tokens at inference. A 2.5M-parameter module iterates over the LLM hidden state, aligns hidden states with input embeddings and supervises each step against the first target semantic-ID token. The module is discarded at deployment. On three Amazon benchmarks, HR@10 improves by 4.0–5.0% relative to a CoT-distilled baseline, with 18.3x lower latency at batch size 1. The useful design is training-only intermediate supervision; the latency result does not establish industrial batched throughput.

zh.text: LatentRec把推荐推理监督放在训练阶段，避免推理时生成额外思维链token。它用一个2.5M参数模块迭代更新LLM隐藏状态，对齐隐藏状态与输入嵌入，并用目标语义ID的首个token监督每一步；部署时移除该模块。在三个Amazon数据集上，相对CoT蒸馏基线，HR@10提高4.0%–5.0%，batch=1时延迟降至约1/18.3。可借鉴的是只在训练时加入中间步骤监督，这一延迟结果不等同于工业批量服务吞吐。

original_abstract.text: Production deployments often use different models to balance cost and quality through cascading, routing, and switching models during long conversations. Context accumulates across turns. Each switch requires the target to repeat prefill over this context. Existing methods transfer full-attention (FA) K/V caches across models. Hybrid linear-attention models also retain recurrent states (REC) and convolution histories (Conv). The interaction between Conv and REC complicates cross-model state transfer. Conv perturbations can change keys and values in recurrent layers and alter REC updates. Conv histories are overwritten, but changes in REC can still affect later outputs. More accurate REC reconstruction need not improve continuation. Building on this, we propose Hybrid State Transfer (HST) for all three state types. It uses structured REC maps and preserves history order during Conv alignment. We calibrate the adapters using the frozen target's outputs during continuation. FA cache map updates are merged offline. Across five benchmarks, Qwen3.5 4B$\rightarrow$27B and 9B$\rightarrow$27B achieve mean task retentions of 89.88% and 94.11%, respectively. With source caches already available, separate timing on synthetic 16K inputs yields handoff body speedups of $21.66\times$ and $21.91\times$.
original_abstract.source_title: Beyond K/V Caches: Cross-Model State Handoff in Hybrid Linear-Attention LLMs

en.text: Hybrid State Transfer handles full-attention caches, recurrent states and convolution histories when switching between hybrid linear-attention models. It uses structured recurrent-state maps, preserves temporal order during convolution alignment and calibrates adapters on the frozen target’s continuation outputs. Qwen3.5 transfer experiments evaluate five benchmarks; separate synthetic-input timings assume source caches already exist. The work identifies state types that a reusable-history interface must preserve, but its handoff speedups are not end-to-end recommendation measurements.

zh.text: Hybrid State Transfer 在混合线性注意力模型切换时，同时处理完整注意力缓存、循环状态和卷积历史。它使用结构化循环状态映射，在卷积对齐中保留时间顺序，并用冻结目标模型的续写输出校准适配器。Qwen3.5 转移实验覆盖五个基准，单独的合成输入计时以源缓存已经存在为前提。该工作明确了复用历史接口需要保留哪些状态，交接加速不能当作推荐服务的端到端收益。

original_abstract.text: We present \textsc{Ginger}, a state-of-the-art open-source C++ library for graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS). We developed \textsc{Ginger} at Google to push the speed and memory efficiency of graph search on large and high-dimensional embedding datasets. \textsc{Ginger} surpasses existing ANNS libraries with regards to query throughput and indexing time while matching the memory footprint of the most space-efficient competitors. \textsc{Ginger} builds upon recent advances in proximity graph construction (PiPNN) and vector quantization (TurboQuant). We introduce Nested TurboQuant (NTQ), a two-level quantizer which supports low precision graph navigation and high precision reranking in a single code. This representation achieves near floating point precision with $2.6\times$ less memory. We also compress the size of our proximity graphs by up to $2.5\times$ without impacting query throughput. We combine graph reordering with a new lossless compression codec called AdaptiveGap, which builds upon StreamVByte. At $95\%$ recall, \textsc{Ginger} speeds up query throughput by an average of $1.8\times$ over each dataset's fastest competitor and by at least $2.3\times$ over any single library. This lead grows to $2.9\times$ over compact libraries on high-dimensional embeddings.
original_abstract.source_title: GINGER: Spicing Up Graph-Based Vector Search

en.text: GINGER improves the speed and memory use of graph-based approximate nearest-neighbor search. Nested TurboQuant stores low-precision navigation and high-precision reranking information in one code, while graph reordering and AdaptiveGap compress graph links. The quantized representation approaches floating-point precision with 2.6x less memory. At 95% recall, query throughput averages 1.8x that of each dataset's fastest competing library. The combination of compact navigation and more precise reranking is directly relevant to large recommendation retrieval indexes; the abstract does not specify benchmark hardware.

zh.text: GINGER优化图近邻检索的速度与内存占用。Nested TurboQuant用同一份编码支持低精度图遍历和高精度重排，图重排序与AdaptiveGap再压缩邻接信息；其量化表示以约1/2.6的内存接近浮点精度。在95%召回率下，查询吞吐平均为各数据集最快对手的1.8倍。把粗检索与精重排所需信息合并存储，可供大规模推荐召回索引参考；摘要未交代测试硬件。

original_abstract.text: Linear attention compresses context into a fixed-size key-value state for linear-time training and constant-memory inference. Gated delta-rule models decay this state and erase its prediction for an incoming key before writing a new value; Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) generalizes this with channel-wise decay and decoupled, full-rank erase and write gates. However, we show that state updates are far less sensitive to erasure than to writes: key activation and unit normalization concentrate key energy onto a sparse subset of channels, whereas value writes scale all channels, so the erase gate can be parameterized at lower rank. Furthermore, slow-decaying state rows accumulate much larger norms than fast rows, dominating unweighted readout and forcing stronger write-time erasure to suppress interference. Guided by this analysis, we introduce Muir, which fuses all gates into a sensitivity-allocated low-rank projection, re-weights state rows with a matched-filter readout gate, and reinvests the saved parameters in a wider feed-forward network. Because standard chunkwise algorithms become numerically unstable at the large chunk sizes needed to saturate wide matrix units, we design a parallel update for stable, efficient training. Across 166M-1.34B parameters, Muir lowers perplexity by 1.8-2.0% over GDN-2 and 2.5-3.6% over Transformer, raises commonsense accuracy by up to 1.9 points, and improves extractive recall over GDN-2. At 1.34B, Muir outperforms both baselines on multi-hop and multi-needle recall, extrapolates 2,560x from its 4K training length to 10M-token streams without perplexity drift, and maintains near-100% passkey retrieval to 1M tokens with static readout. Muir achieves these gains while matching GDN-2 throughput, reaching its 100B-token validation loss 1.2x faster, and training 2.7x faster than Transformer at 32K.
original_abstract.source_title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout

en.text: Muir addresses uneven sensitivity in linear-attention erase and write gates and interference from slow-decaying state rows. It combines low-rank gate projections, a matched-filter readout and a numerically stable parallel update, reallocating saved parameters to the feed-forward network. Across 166M–1.34B models, it reports 1.8–2.0% lower perplexity than GDN-2 while matching its throughput; at 32K context, training is 2.7x faster than Transformer. Its 1.34B model also extrapolates from 4K training sequences to 10M-token streams without perplexity drift. Sensitivity-aware state updates offer a direction for long-history recommendation, which is not evaluated here.

zh.text: Muir针对线性注意力中擦除与写入门的敏感度差异，以及慢衰减状态行主导读出的问题，采用低秩门投影、匹配滤波读出和数值稳定的并行更新，把省下的参数用于加宽前馈网络。在166M–1.34B模型上，相对GDN-2困惑度降低1.8%–2.0%，吞吐相当；32K上下文下训练速度为Transformer的2.7倍。1.34B模型还能从4K训练长度外推到10M token流，未出现困惑度漂移。按敏感度分配状态更新容量可供长行为历史建模参考，论文未验证推荐任务。

original_abstract.text: User embeddings are central components of modern recommendation, personalization, and behavioral modeling systems. Though these embeddings can compactly encode rich behavioral information, they are inherently dense and opaque, limiting interpretability. To address this gap, we argue that user embeddings can be understood as sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes. This structure is directly predicted by generative models of user behavior for linear embeddings and extends approximately to deep-learning representations by the superposition hypothesis. Superimposed modes can naturally be recovered by sparse dictionary learning methods, such as sparse autoencoders (SAEs), and recovered modes can be automatically named and queried in natural language. We validate mode recovery against known ground truth on synthetic data, where SAEs recover modes better than classical sparse baselines. We then apply our methods to classical and transformer-based user embeddings from two real-world datasets. We also show how the corresponding natural-language labels enable zero-shot audience retrieval and characterization over embeddings never trained on text. The framework is post-hoc and model-agnostic, requiring no modification to the upstream embedding system.
original_abstract.source_title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes

en.text: The paper treats user embeddings as superpositions of sparse behavioral modes. Sparse dictionary learning, including sparse autoencoders, recovers modes that can be named and queried in natural language. Synthetic experiments test recovery against known ground truth, while two real datasets cover classical and transformer-based user representations. The labels support zero-shot audience retrieval over embeddings not trained on text. This post-hoc interface may make shared user representations easier to inspect and reuse without changing the upstream model; it does not establish a ranking lift.

zh.text: 论文将用户嵌入看作稀疏行为模式的叠加，用稀疏自编码器等字典学习方法恢复模式，再为其生成可用自然语言查询的名称。合成实验检验已知模式能否恢复，两个真实数据集覆盖传统和 Transformer 用户表示；这些标签还能支持对未用文本训练的嵌入进行零样本人群检索。它为共享用户表示提供了无需改动上游模型的解释与复用接口，但没有证明排序收益。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation has shown considerable potential in industrial recommendation systems. However, the performance of existing generative methods is limited by several challenges. 1) Semantic IDs (SIDs) are treated as one-dimensional sequences, overlooking the hierarchical dependencies among different layers. 2) Next-token prediction used is unable to explicitly optimize session-wise recommendation. 3) Although reinforcement learning has been applied to align generated recommendations with user preferences, few existing methods explicitly optimize the ranking of positive items in session-wise recommendation. To address the above issues, we propose RedMall, a generative recommender designed for large-scale e-commerce. Firstly, RedMall constructs hierarchical SIDs through residual quantization over multimodal representations. Secondly, RedMall introduces a lightweight SID encoder to explicitly model layer-wise dependencies in SIDs. Moreover, RedMall incorporates sparse mixture-of-experts, dual gated attention, and multi-target prediction to scale model size, enhance user interest representation, and optimize session-wise recommendation. We further design an exposure-aware loss that treats exposed but unclicked items as negative feedback. To better align user preferences and list-wise ranking objectives, we combine Group Relative Policy Optimization with an auxiliary LambdaRank loss, using both real user feedback and item ranking to guide optimization. Experiments on four public datasets-Amazon Beauty, Amazon Toys, Amazon Food, and MovieLens-1M---show that RedMall outperforms the evaluated baselines across all reported Recall and NDCG metrics. Online A/B tests show improvements of 2.24% in advertiser value (ADVV) and 0.59% in click-through rate (CTR) for e-commerce advertising, as well as gains of 1.08% in GMV and 0.95% in daily active buyers (DAB) for e-commerce recommendations.
original_abstract.source_title: RedMall: Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale E-commerce

en.text: RedMall combines hierarchical semantic IDs with a lightweight ID encoder, sparse experts, dual gated attention and multi-target prediction for large-scale e-commerce recommendation. Exposure-aware training uses unclicked impressions as negative feedback; group-relative policy optimization and an auxiliary LambdaRank loss align generated lists with user feedback and item order. It outperforms the evaluated baselines on four public datasets. Online tests report 2.24% higher advertiser value and 0.59% higher CTR for advertising, plus 1.08% higher GMV for recommendations. It provides a concrete architecture and training recipe for scaling generative recommendation; these gains belong to the reported deployment settings.

zh.text: RedMall 用分层语义 ID 表示商品，再结合轻量 ID 编码器、稀疏专家、双门控注意力和多目标预测扩展电商推荐。训练把曝光未点击作为负反馈，并结合组相对策略优化与 LambdaRank 损失，让生成结果兼顾用户反馈和列表顺序。四个公开数据集上优于所比较基线；线上广告实验报告广告主价值提升 2.24%、CTR 提升 0.59%，推荐场景 GMV 提升 1.08%。它提供了生成式推荐扩模的架构与训练方案，收益限于论文所测部署条件。

original_abstract.text: Large language models (LLMs) are attractive rerankers for recommendation. Running an expensive model on every request is costly, and for users with sparse interaction histories it often lowers quality. We present CascadeRec, a two-tier LLM reranking cascade deployed in production at a large financial planning and analysis (FP&A) SaaS provider. It serves content recommendations to enterprise tenants on AWS EKS and GKE. A lightweight Tier-1 model reranks every request. A router escalates only the requests where extra inference-time compute is likely to help, and sends them to a more expensive Tier-2 procedure (self-consistency sampling, multi-path reasoning, or a larger model). The system has run in a production A/B experiment for over a month. Compared with uniform use of the expensive tier, CascadeRec has reduced inference cost by about 10%, with minimal latency impact and no quality regression observed to date. Tenant data cannot be released, so we also evaluate the pipeline on public benchmarks (MovieLens-1M and Amazon-Electronics). Segment-level analysis with paired-bootstrap confidence intervals shows that uniform LLM reranking lowers NDCG@10 for sparse-history users by up to 30%, and its only statistically significant gain appears on the segment with the longest histories. Escalating cold users can make the loss larger instead of repairing it. Which segments benefit from escalation depends on the domain, and this motivates the segment-gated rollout we use in production. We describe the deployment architecture, the measured benefits, and lessons learned, including inter-tenant load imbalance as a driver for cascading and the handling of LLM output-parsing failures at the serving layer.
original_abstract.source_title: CascadeRec: Deployed Adaptive LLM Compute Allocation for Multi-Tenant Content Recommendation

en.text: CascadeRec runs a lightweight LLM reranker on every request and routes only promising requests to a more expensive model or reasoning procedure. A production A/B experiment lasting over a month reports about 10% lower inference cost than uniformly using the expensive tier, with minimal latency impact and no observed quality regression so far. Public MovieLens and Amazon experiments show that extra LLM computation can instead harm sparse-history users. The practical lesson for ranking compute allocation is to measure benefit by user segment and domain before escalation, rather than treating more inference as uniformly helpful.

zh.text: CascadeRec 先用轻量大模型重排所有请求，只把预计能受益的请求交给更贵的模型或推理过程。持续一个多月的生产 A/B 实验中，相比统一使用昂贵层，推理成本约降 10%，延迟变化较小，暂未观察到质量退化。MovieLens 和 Amazon 实验则发现，额外的大模型计算可能伤害历史稀疏用户。它为排序计算分配提供了具体做法：先按用户群和业务验证收益，再决定哪些请求值得升级推理。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation aims to predict item identifiers from user interaction histories, but explicit control over the properties of recommended items remains underexplored. A key challenge is to connect human-readable concepts to internal features whose interventions effectively change the recommended items. To address this, we propose Steerable Generative Recommender (SteerGR), a framework that uses sparse autoencoders for concept-level control in game discovery. SteerGR proceeds through three stages: (i) Concept Definition and Grounding for defining play concepts with an LLM; (ii) Feature Discovery and Selection for discovering candidate features by their concept associations and selecting one by its steering effect; and (iii) Sparse Feature Intervention for amplifying or suppressing selected features to steer recommendations without retraining the recommender. Extensive experiments with two industrial generative recommendation models on a real-world game dataset show that the selected features successfully steer recommendations toward or away from target concepts. We believe this work takes a first step to extend SAE-based steering from LLMs to industrial generative recommendation.
original_abstract.source_title: SteerGR: Steering Generative Recommendation via Sparse Autoencoders for Controllable Game Discovery

en.text: SteerGR makes generative game recommendations controllable through sparse-autoencoder features. It first grounds human-readable play concepts, then finds associated internal features and selects them by their measured steering effect. Amplifying or suppressing selected features changes recommendations without retraining the recommender. Experiments use two industrial generative models on a real game dataset and show movement toward or away from target concepts. This adds a concept-level control interface to a shared recommendation model; it does not establish a scaling law or an online business lift.

zh.text: SteerGR 用稀疏自编码器特征控制生成式游戏推荐。它先把可读的游戏概念与内容对应起来，再寻找相关内部特征，按实际引导效果选择干预对象；放大或抑制这些特征即可改变推荐，无需重新训练推荐模型。两个工业生成模型在真实游戏数据上的实验表明，推荐结果可以朝目标概念靠近或远离。可借鉴点是给共享推荐模型增加概念级控制接口，论文未建立扩展规律，也未证明线上业务收益。

original_abstract.text: Search and recommendation at Shopify require retrieving relevant products from a changing catalog of billions of products under strict latency constraints. We present SID-LLM, which casts both tasks as generating semantic IDs: short sequences of content-derived tokens representing products. We jointly pre-train SID-LLM on catalog and behavioral data, giving search and recommendation a shared representation and training objective. We show that reinforcement learning further improves judged search relevance. Furthermore, distillation from task-specific experts improves recommendation quality over joint supervised fine-tuning without a statistically detected loss in search quality. Finally, for efficient serving, we pair multi-token prediction with a lightweight ranker, improving retrieval quality over our autoregressive baseline while reducing latency. We evaluate SID-LLM both as a standalone retriever and as a component of Shopify's production search and recommendation systems. As a standalone search system, SID-LLM achieves quality comparable to Shopify's existing multi-model search stack while meeting production latency requirements. Integrating SID-LLM into the search and recommendation stacks provides significant gains in both offline evaluations and online A/B tests. Together, these results demonstrate the practical value of semantic-ID generation as a unified approach to product discovery at scale.
original_abstract.source_title: Generative Search and Recommendation at Shopify

en.text: SID-LLM unifies product search and recommendation as generation of short content-derived semantic IDs over a changing catalog of billions of products. Joint catalog-and-behavior pretraining supplies a shared representation; reinforcement learning improves judged search relevance, while task-expert distillation improves recommendation without a statistically detected search-quality loss. Multi-token prediction with a lightweight ranker improves retrieval quality and latency over the autoregressive baseline. Standalone search quality is comparable to the existing multi-model stack; production integration reports offline and online gains. It offers an industrial example of sharing a generative backbone while addressing task interference and serving cost.

zh.text: SID-LLM 把搜索与推荐统一为生成商品语义 ID，服务不断变化的数十亿商品目录。商品内容与行为数据联合预训练提供共享表示；强化学习改善搜索相关性，任务专家蒸馏提升推荐质量，且未检测到搜索质量的显著下降。服务端结合多 token 预测和轻量排序器，相比逐 token 生成基线改善检索质量与延迟。独立搜索质量接近现有多模型方案，接入生产系统后报告离线和线上收益，可借鉴其共享骨干、处理任务干扰并控制服务成本的做法。

original_abstract.text: Quantization-aware training (QAT) is the most reliable way to obtain accurate low-bit large language models (LLMs), but training with AdamW keeps two dense FP32 states for every weight matrix. We find that low-rank memory-efficient optimizers such as GaLore and LDAdam degrade substantially in QAT. A considerable part of the QAT momentum lies outside its top-r singular subspace, and projection-based methods discard this part at every step. We further observe that this residual remains useful when only its sign is kept. Based on these observations, we propose ResQAdam. It keeps a single BF16 momentum, applies Adam only to the r x r coordinates of the principal subspace, and adds a normalized sign update computed from the residual. We evaluate ResQAdam with two from-scratch QAT methods and three QAT fine-tuning pipelines, with weights quantized down to 2 bits. It reduces optimizer-state memory by 71% to 74% relative to AdamW, stays close to AdamW in most settings, and lowers training throughput by less than 2%.
original_abstract.source_title: ResQAdam: Residual-Preserving Adaptive Optimization for Memory-Efficient Quantization Aware Training

en.text: ResQAdam targets the optimizer-state cost of quantization-aware training. It retains one BF16 momentum tensor, applies Adam updates within a low-dimensional principal subspace, and preserves information outside that subspace through a normalized residual-sign update. This addresses the loss of useful momentum caused by repeatedly discarding low-rank projection residuals. Across from-scratch and fine-tuning QAT pipelines, including weights down to two bits, the authors report 71–74% lower optimizer-state memory than AdamW with less than 2% training-throughput reduction. The memory accounting excludes embeddings and the output head; these are optimizer-state savings, not total training-memory savings. Benefits for large recommendation models remain untested.

zh.text: ResQAdam 面向量化感知训练的优化器显存开销，保留一份 BF16 动量，在低维主子空间内执行 Adam 更新，并用归一化残差符号补回投影外的信息，避免低秩方法反复丢弃有效动量。论文覆盖从头训练和微调式量化，最低至二比特权重；报告相对 AdamW 减少 71%–74% 的优化器状态显存，训练吞吐下降低于 2%。显存统计不含嵌入与输出头，该数字不等于总训练显存降幅，大规模推荐模型上的收益仍待验证。

original_abstract.text: Latent reasoning in generative recommendation faces two practical barriers: constructing teacher-generated chain-of-thought (CoT) supervision is costly, and recurrent hidden-state feedback requires a specialized execution loop. We revisit both the supervision source and the computation interface. A step-level diagnosis measures how recommendation CoT supports next-item prediction and trace coherence. In the analyzed traces, history analysis is the only step with positive mean contributions on both dimensions, while later preference and intent steps have negative mean answer contributions. Guided by this finding, we propose PHiT (Prefilled, History-Informed Thought Tokens), which learns intermediate states from semantic targets extracted directly from observed item histories. PHiT aggregates cached sparse item encodings to construct these targets and supervises the contextual states of distinct vocabulary thought tokens. All thought tokens are supplied together as ordinary input IDs during a single causal prefill, removing the need for recurrent final-state feedback. With supervised fine-tuning alone, PHiT outperforms the compared baselines across four recommendation benchmarks. Controlled ablations support the value of input-matched semantic supervision, while cost measurements show fast target construction with training time comparable to the recommendation-only thought-token baseline.
original_abstract.source_title: Rethinking Latent Reasoning for Generative Recommendation: Beyond Teacher-Generated CoT and Recurrent Hidden-State Feedback

en.text: PHiT reduces two costs of latent reasoning for recommendation: teacher-generated chain-of-thought supervision and recurrent hidden-state feedback. It derives semantic targets directly from cached sparse item encodings in observed histories, then supervises distinct thought-token states. All thought tokens enter a single causal prefill as ordinary input IDs. Supervised fine-tuning outperforms the compared baselines on four recommendation benchmarks, with training time comparable to the recommendation-only thought-token baseline. The useful design choice is to align intermediate supervision with available history while retaining a conventional inference interface.

zh.text: PHiT 针对推荐隐式推理的两项开销：生成教师思维链，以及循环回传隐藏状态。它直接聚合用户历史中缓存的稀疏商品编码，构造语义监督目标；不同思考 token 一次性作为普通输入进入因果预填充。仅用监督微调便在四个推荐基准上优于所比较方法，训练时间与只做推荐训练的思考 token 基线相近。它把中间监督对齐到已有历史信息，同时保留常规推理接口，可供低成本推理增强推荐参考。

original_abstract.text: Expert-parallel mixture-of-experts (MoE) layers run at the pace of the most loaded GPU, and a few hot experts carry most of the excess load. Replicating them at every MoE layer balances the load only if their weights arrive within the layer, and broadcasting from the owner is the bottleneck: point-to-point copies overload it, and baseline broadcasts pay latency or bandwidth overheads. We present ISER-MoE (In-Switch Expert Replication for MoE), built in TensorRT-LLM, which multicasts hot experts through the NVLink switch to fixed GPU groups, so each byte leaves its owner once. A GPU scheduler assigns hot experts to groups per layer, and a multi-port broadcast spreads the injection over the group's ports, both overlapped with the shared expert. In trace replay, the scheduler removed 98-99% of the excess load; in prefill serving of DeepSeek-V4-Pro, throughput rose 17.4% on a math benchmark and 7.2% on agentic prompts.
original_abstract.source_title: ISER-MoE: Dynamic In-Switch Replication of Hot Experts for Load Balancing in Expert-Parallel

en.text: ISER-MoE replicates hot experts through NVLink-switch multicast to balance expert-parallel inference without repeatedly sending each expert's weights from its owner. A GPU scheduler assigns hot experts to fixed groups, while multi-port broadcasts overlap with shared-expert computation. Trace replay removes 98–99% of excess load; DeepSeek-V4-Pro prefill throughput improves by 17.4% on a math benchmark and 7.2% on agentic prompts. Dynamic replication and communication overlap could inform large MoE recommendation serving, but the results concern language-model inference.

zh.text: ISER-MoE通过NVLink交换机组播复制热门专家，避免权重持有者反复发送同一份数据，以缓解专家并行推理的负载不均。GPU调度器将热门专家分配到固定组，多端口广播再与共享专家计算重叠。轨迹回放中消除了98–99%的超额负载；DeepSeek-V4-Pro的prefill吞吐在数学基准和智能体提示上分别提高17.4%和7.2%。动态复制与通信重叠可供大规模MoE推荐服务参考，但实验对象是语言模型推理。

original_abstract.text:
Multi-vector retrieval represents each query and document as a set of embeddings and scores relevance via fine-grained set-to-set interactions such as MaxSim (Chamfer similarity). This expressiveness improves retrieval quality over single-vector representations, but makes search substantially more expensive. Existing systems address this challenge primarily through proxy representations or filter-and-rerank pipelines that reduce candidate generation to single-vector search. We study the complementary direction of building a native IVF-style index directly over multi-vector data.
We introduce MV-IVF, an inverted-file index for multi-vector retrieval built on MV-Lloyd, a new Lloyd-style algorithm for clustering point clouds under a Chamfer objective. Our key observation is that once point clouds are assigned to clusters, the center-update step reduces to standard single-vector clustering over the flattened embeddings in each cluster. This enables efficient construction of a hierarchical IVF tree with center point clouds at internal nodes.
At query time, MV-IVF performs best-first beam search over the tree to identify promising leaf clusters, then scores the documents in those leaves. We further accelerate search using low-bit quantization, query compression, and cache-efficient batched search. We implement MV-IVF in MVSIC, an optimized C++ library and unified evaluation framework for multi-vector retrieval that includes several major approaches. Across BEIR and LoTTE text retrieval benchmarks, MV-IVF achieves strong latency--recall tradeoffs, the best batched throughput frontiers, and favorable build-time and index-size profiles. At $90\%$ Recall-$10$@$10$, MV-IVF achieves up to $8.03\times$ lower single-query latency and up to $173.5\times$ higher QPS than the baselines, demonstrating that native IVF-style indexing is practical and effective for scalable multi-vector retrieval.
original_abstract.source_title: MV-IVF: Multi-Vector Retrieval via Multi-Vector Clustering

en.text: MV-IVF builds an inverted-file index directly over multi-vector representations. Its MV-Lloyd clustering turns center updates into ordinary clustering over flattened embeddings, producing a hierarchical tree of point-cloud centers. Search traverses promising leaves, with low-bit quantization, query compression and cache-efficient batching reducing cost. On BEIR and LoTTE, the reported comparisons show strong latency–recall and batched-throughput tradeoffs. The transferable idea is to index the multi-vector scoring structure itself rather than only using a single-vector proxy; benefits for recommendation retrieval require separate validation.

zh.text: MV-IVF 直接为多向量表示建立倒排索引。MV-Lloyd 聚类把中心更新转成对展开后的向量做普通聚类，从而构建以向量集合为中心的层次树；查询优先访问有希望的叶节点，再配合低比特量化、查询压缩和批量访问减少开销。BEIR 与 LoTTE 实验报告较好的延迟—召回率和吞吐权衡。它为多兴趣、多向量召回提供了直接索引思路，但推荐场景收益仍需单独验证。

original_abstract.text: The context lengths of large language models (LLMs) are rapidly increasing in real-world applications such as agentic systems and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). To accelerate LLM inference in these scenarios, reusing position-independent key-value (KV) caches across requests has emerged as a promising approach. This technique typically relies on recomputing a selected subset of tokens to restore cross-chunk interactions. However, existing solutions suffer from critical limitations in both algorithmic efficiency and system deployment. Algorithmically, they overlook the distribution of KV cache deviations, leading to either high token-selection overhead or degraded generation quality. At the system level, the reliance on custom LLM execution flows for recomputation complicates deployment and prevents seamless integration with highly optimized inference engines. In this paper, we propose DARIC (\textbf{D}istribution-\textbf{A}ware \textbf{R}ecomputation for \textbf{I}ndependent KV \textbf{C}ache Reuse), a novel KV cache reuse method based on system-algorithm co-design. At its core, DARIC introduces a distribution-aware token selection strategy that adaptively schedules token recomputation based on empirical KV deviation patterns, striking an optimal balance between generation quality and computational efficiency. Moreover, DARIC is built on a lightweight system architecture that enables independent KV cache generation and recomputation with minimal integration overhead, fully preserving existing system-level optimizations of standard inference engines. Comprehensive experiments across various datasets and LLMs demonstrate that DARIC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving a 1.1$\times$--4.5$\times$ speedup in time-to-first-token (TTFT) with negligible loss in generation quality. Code is available at this https URL.
original_abstract.source_title: DARIC: A Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse System with Distribution-Aware Recomputation

en.text: DARIC reuses position-independent KV caches while selectively recomputing tokens to restore interactions between cached chunks. Its selection rule follows observed distributions of cache deviations, balancing recomputation overhead against generation quality. A lightweight system design aims to preserve existing inference-engine optimizations rather than requiring a separate execution path. Across the evaluated language models and datasets, the paper reports faster time to first token with little quality loss. Reusing shared content or user-history segments could be useful for generative recommendation, but the applicable sharing patterns, cache-management costs, and recommendation quality have not been established.

zh.text: DARIC 复用与位置无关的 KV 缓存，并选择性重算部分 token，恢复缓存片段之间的交互。选择规则依据观测到的缓存偏差分布，权衡重算开销与生成质量；轻量系统设计尽量保留现有推理引擎优化，避免另建执行流程。论文在所测语言模型和数据集上报告首 token 延迟下降、质量损失较小。该方法可启发共享内容或用户历史片段的复用，但哪些推荐请求能有效共享、缓存管理成本多大、质量是否稳定，仍需专门验证。

original_abstract.text: Low-precision matrix throughput on modern GPUs is growing far faster than vector-arithmetic throughput. Attention therefore cannot realize the available GEMM performance because softmax has become the pipeline bottleneck. We introduce Fused-Softmax Attention, a training-free algorithm that reformulates and approximates softmax to fold its dominant operations into the attention GEMMs, moving work from vector units to matrix cores. Implemented for the AMD CDNA 4 architecture, our MXFP8, MXFP6 and MXFP4 kernels reach approximately 3.0, 4.0 and 4.6 PFLOP/s on an AMD Instinct MI355X GPU, yielding speedups of $2.1\times$, $2.8\times$ and $3.2\times$ over the BF16 attention. Importantly, the additional error introduced by Fused-Softmax remains below the error floor set by quantizing the GEMM operands. On Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, a hybrid MXFP6/4 schedule delivers up to $2.05\times$ end-to-end speedup while preserving the visual quality of the outputs. The kernels ship in AMD's open-source AITER library, and they powered AMD's MLPerf Inference v6.1 Wan2.2 submission, which ran $1.7\times$ faster than AMD's previous-round result on the same hardware. Our results show that redesigning softmax to utilize the matrix pipeline enables attention to capitalize on continued growth in low-precision matrix throughput.
original_abstract.source_title: Fused-Softmax for efficient quantized attention

en.text: Fused-Softmax redesigns approximate softmax for quantized attention so more work runs on matrix cores instead of vector units. AMD CDNA 4 kernels cover MXFP8, MXFP6 and MXFP4, with additional approximation error below the tested operand-quantization error. Wan2.2 video-generation experiments provide an end-to-end evaluation alongside kernel benchmarks. The system illustrates how low-bit attention requires joint arithmetic and kernel design; gains on recommendation models remain unverified.

zh.text: Fused-Softmax 为量化注意力重新设计近似 softmax，将更多运算从向量单元转移到矩阵核心。AMD CDNA 4 实现覆盖 MXFP8、MXFP6 和 MXFP4，所测附加近似误差小于操作数量化误差；除内核测试外，论文还用 Wan2.2 视频生成评估端到端效果。它说明低比特注意力需要协同设计算法与内核，推荐模型上的收益仍待验证。
